rationale: Every method tested on the seven-test v2 family failed at 96 months, with failures concentrated in persistent effect series. The 63- and 252-session horizons overlap across monthly origins by construction, which creates that persistence. A family restricted to 21-session horizons evaluated at monthly origins has no overlap by construction. This study checks whether familywise error is then controlled, keeping the high-persistence scenarios in the grid so that the redesign is not assumed to remove them.

arms.p_value: one-sided Student t with n-1 degrees of freedom
arms.purpose: the test justified when monthly 21-session effects are serially independent

arms.statistic: Bartlett with M = n-1 (fixed-b, b = 1), as in docs/estudio-calibracion-fixed-b-v1.json
arms.p_value: (1 + #{reference >= t}) / (1 + draws) with a new reference of 100000 Gaussian series of length 1200

synthetic_data.generator: the AR(1) common-factor generator of scripts/confirmatory_hac_stress.py with three columns instead of seven

calibration_evaluation.interval_method: Clopper-Pearson bilateral with Bonferroni over both arms and 64 scenarios
calibration_evaluation.excess_evidence_rule: any simultaneous lower bound > 0.05 in an arm
calibration_evaluation.primary_reading: scenarios with AR(1) 0 and 0.3 represent the non-overlapping design; 0.6 and 0.85 are kept as stress and reported separately

activation.next_step_if_controlled: a separate v3 confirmatory registration with power analysis and economic effect sizes before any new cohort
